deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It has three parts.

(1) Top: a continuation of Gauss's running list 'Neue Bücher von 1821', carried over from the previous page. It names:
- J. Oxley, Journals of two expeditions into the interior of New South Wales, 1817–1818 (London 1820).
- Gergonne, Annales de mathématiques pures et appliquées, tome XI nos. 1–6 and tome XII nos. 1–2 (1822).
- Delambre, Histoire de l'astronomie moderne, tomes 1–2 (1821).
- 'Marcoz' (written like 'Mariotz/Marioz'), Remarques critiques sur l'histoire de l'astronomie ancienne de Delambre (1819). This is J.-B.-P. Marcoz, a known polemical critic of Delambre. In the first line Gauss wrote 'l'astronomie', struck it and replaced it with 'l'histoire'.

(2) Middle: an administrative log for early 1822. It almost certainly concerns the Hanoverian degree measurement (Gradmessung) and its government funding. Planet and moon signs give the weekdays.
- 'Bericht abgesandt' (report sent): ☾ = Monday, 7 Jan 1822.
- Report on the heights sent to the Kammer: Monday, 14 Jan.
- Last remittance of 50 Louis d'or ('Lsd') received: ♃ = Thursday, 17 Jan.
- Accounts sent to the C.M. (Cabinets-Ministerium): ♀ = Friday, 18 Jan.
- Rescript of the C.M. dated February, received February.
- Remainder of the money, 100 Louis d'or, received February.
- Report to the C.M. concerning the continuation of the work in 1822 sent: Monday, 11 March.

(3) Bottom, added later: '1828. 1 febr. ♀ Morg. 11^u'. That is Friday 1 Feb 1828, 11 a.m., the publication of a priority judgment ('Prioritäts-Urtheil'). The adjective before it reads roughly 'Br[e/o]den-schen' and cannot be identified with confidence.

No derivation is present, so nothing can be reconstructed mathematically. My one inference is the weekday check: I computed the dates against the weekday symbols, and all of them are consistent.

checkable.asserts: Total of the two remittances recorded, in Louis d'or

transcription_corrections: 'Mariotz[?]' is most likely 'Marcoz' (J.-B.-P. Marcoz, author of 'Remarques critiques sur l'histoire de l'astronomie ancienne de M. Delambre').
'Lond. 1820[?]' is consistent with the actual London 1820 edition of Oxley's Journals.
'Lsd' should be read as Louis d'or, not pounds sterling.
The name before 'Prioritäts Urtheils' looks closer to 'Bro/Bre-den-schen' than 'Breda-schen' and remains uncertain.
In the Marcoz entry, 'astronomie' after 'sur l'' is struck and replaced by 'l'histoire'.
